changes.old: For those matters (e.g., personal injury) and clients (e.g., individuals) where an `Industry` is not applicable.
changes.new: An industry classification for matters where the primary client is a natural person rather than an incorporated entity, partnership, or other formal business structure. Used for personal legal matters including estate planning, high-net-worth advisory, family law, and work involving influencers, athletes, or other individuals whose economic activity does not fit a single corporate sector code.

Cultivation, on-site processing, and extraction of cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.) for commercial purposes, covering medical cannabis, recreational cannabis, and industrial hemp. Encompasses the full point-of-production cycle: growing from seed or clone through harvest (indoor, greenhouse, and outdoor operations); post-harvest processing including drying, curing, and trimming; and primary extraction of cannabinoids and other plant-derived compounds. Also includes nurseries supplying genetics and clones to other cultivators. Excludes wholesale distribution, retail dispensary operations, and the manufacture of finished consumer products incorporating cannabis-derived inputs.

Software that automates general business functions used across most industries — including finance and accounting, enterprise resource planning, customer relationship management, human capital management, sales, marketing, advertising, e-commerce, customer service, productivity, and collaboration. Examples include SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, HubSpot, Workday, and ServiceNow.

Software whose primary product is built for the operations, regulatory profile, or workflows of a specific industry rather than for cross-industry use. Covers verticals such as healthcare, legal, financial services, insurance, real estate, government, education, hospitality, construction, manufacturing, logistics, retail, and energy. Examples include Epic (healthcare), Veeva (life sciences), Toast (restaurants), Clio (legal), and Procore (construction).

Software that supports the development, deployment, operation, and integration of other software, including operating systems, databases, application development platforms, developer tools, DevOps and site-reliability software, observability and monitoring, and integration middleware. Examples include Linux distributions, PostgreSQL, GitHub, GitLab, Datadog, and MuleSoft. Excludes underlying compute, storage, and network services, which are classified under Computing Infrastructure Providers (NAICS 5182).

Software whose primary function is to protect computer systems, networks, applications, identities, and data from unauthorized access, misuse, or attack. Includes endpoint and network security, cloud and application security, identity and access management, security operations (SIEM/SOAR), encryption and data protection, and fraud, anti-money-laundering, and compliance software. Examples include CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Okta, SentinelOne, and Splunk.

Software for storing, processing, analyzing, and modeling data — including business intelligence and analytics, data warehousing and data lakes, data integration and ETL, machine learning platforms (MLOps), foundation model providers, and applied AI and AI agent platforms. Examples include Snowflake, Databricks, Tableau, Hugging Face, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

Software used to design, simulate, model, and document physical products, structures, systems, and spatial environments — including computer-aided design (CAD), computer-aided manufacturing and engineering (CAM/CAE), electronic design automation (EDA), simulation, and geographic information systems (GIS). Examples include Autodesk, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, Ansys, and Esri.

Software whose primary buyers are individual consumers rather than businesses or institutions, including mobile applications, social and communication apps, dating and lifestyle apps, and personal productivity tools. Examples include Spotify, Duolingo, WhatsApp, and Strava. Excludes consumer video games, which are classified under NAICS 5132.
